body.statement: Suppose \(m\) is odd and no allowed edge \(j\to i\) has \(A_{ii}=A_{jj}=0\). Then every nonempty \(\mathcal S(B,Q;G)\) is a singleton. Its diagonal is \(A_{ii}=B_{ii}^{1/m}\); its allowed off-diagonal entries are recovered in increasing endpoint gap by \(A_{ij}=\{B_{ij}-R_{ij,m}(A)\}/C_m(A_{ii},A_{jj})\); and its diagonal innovations are recovered in increasing \(i\) by \(D_{ii}=\{Q_{ii}-\sum_{j<i}D_{jj}\sum_{r=0}^{m-1}(A^r)_{ij}^2\}/\sum_{r=0}^{m-1}A_{ii}^{2r}\). For arbitrary \((B,Q)\), the recursively produced candidate is compatible if and only if its diagonal is stable, every recovered \(D_{ii}\) is positive, every forbidden entry of \(A^m=B\) holds, and the complete covariance equation \(Q=\sum_{r=0}^{m-1}A^rD(A^r)^\top\) holds. Consequently every nonempty compatible transfer fiber satisfies \(\mathcal H_{uv}(B,Q;G)=\{h_{uv}\}\).
body.justification: This is the constructive point-identification half of the parity frontier.
body.gap: Gong et al. require non-Gaussian shocks for recovery; Smith computes a chosen root but does not prove uniqueness after graph and innovation-covariance checks.
body.consumer: Fine-grid policy or scientific impulse analysis can use a closed-form transfer even though only every \(m\)-th state was recorded.
body.proof_tex:
Let \((A,D)\in\mathcal S(B,Q;G)\).  Because a triangular matrix and each of its powers have diagonal entries equal to the corresponding powers of the original diagonal entries,
\[
 B_{ii}=(A^m)_{ii}=A_{ii}^m.
\]
The map \(x\mapsto x^m\) is one-to-one on \(\mathbb R\) for odd \(m\), so necessarily
\[
 A_{ii}=B_{ii}^{1/m}
\]
for every \(i\).  Thus every compatible pair has the same diagonal transition coefficients.

Proceed by induction on the endpoint gap \(g=i-j\ge1\).  All entries of gap zero have just been determined.  Suppose all allowed entries of gap less than \(g\) have been determined.  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}path\mbox{-}expansion}\) gives, for an allowed edge \(j\to i\) of gap \(g\),
\[
 B_{ij}=A_{ij}C_m(A_{ii},A_{jj})+R_{ij,m}(A).
\]
Every off-diagonal factor in \(R_{ij,m}(A)\) has gap less than \(g\), so the induction hypothesis determines the remainder.  By the hypothesis on allowed edges and Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}divided\mbox{-}difference\mbox{-}zero\mbox{-}set}\),
\[
 C_m(A_{ii},A_{jj})>0.
\]
Division is therefore valid and forces
\[
 A_{ij}=\frac{B_{ij}-R_{ij,m}(A)}{C_m(A_{ii},A_{jj})}.
\]
For a forbidden pair, graph support forces \(A_{ij}=0\), and the same path expansion turns the equality \(A^m=B\) at that coordinate into the check \(B_{ij}=R_{ij,m}(A)\).  Induction over \(g=1,\ldots,d-1\) proves that there is at most one graph-compatible \(A\) and gives the asserted recursion.

Fix this \(A\).  Since \(D\) is diagonal, the \((i,i)\) entry of the coarse covariance equation is
\[
 Q_{ii}
 =\sum_{r=0}^{m-1}\sum_{j=1}^{d}D_{jj}(A^r)_{ij}^{2}.
\]
Lower triangularity gives \((A^r)_{ij}=0\) for \(j>i\), while \((A^r)_{ii}=A_{ii}^r\).  Hence
\[
 Q_{ii}
 =D_{ii}\sum_{r=0}^{m-1}A_{ii}^{2r}
  +\sum_{j<i}D_{jj}\sum_{r=0}^{m-1}(A^r)_{ij}^{2}.
\]
The coefficient of \(D_{ii}\) is at least its \(r=0\) term, namely one.  Starting at \(i=1\) and increasing \(i\), division therefore uniquely yields exactly the displayed innovation recursion.  Thus there is at most one diagonal \(D\).

For sufficiency, construct \(A\) and \(D\) by these recursions.  The diagonal and allowed-coordinate equations for \(A^m=B\) hold by construction; imposing the forbidden-coordinate checks gives the full equation \(A^m=B\).  The diagonal covariance equations hold by construction; imposing the remaining entries gives the full equation \(Q=\sum_{r=0}^{m-1}A^rD(A^r)^\top\).  The graph zeros are built into \(A\).  The explicit stability and positivity checks give \(\max_i|A_{ii}|<1\) and diagonal \(D\succ0\), respectively.  These are precisely all conditions in \(\mathcal S(B,Q;G)\), proving sufficiency.  Necessity of each check follows immediately from the definition of that fiber.  It follows that every nonempty fiber is a singleton.

Finally, \(\mathcal H_{uv}(B,Q;G)\) is the image of the compatible fiber under
\[
 (A,D)\longmapsto \left[z\longmapsto\frac{A_{vu}z}{1-A_{vv}z}\right].
\]
Stability gives \(|A_{vv}z|<1\) for \(|z|=1\), so the denominator never vanishes.  The singleton parameter fiber therefore maps to the singleton containing the causal transfer \(h_{uv}\), rather than defining that causal transfer from the observed law.

For an exact two-node stress test satisfying the regularity condition, take \(m=3\),
\[
 A=\begin{pmatrix}1/2&0\\1/4&1/3\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad D=I_2.
\]
Then \(B_{11}=1/8\), \(B_{22}=1/27\), and, since there is no indirect path,
\[
 B_{21}=\frac14 C_3(1/3,1/2)
 =\frac14\left(\frac19+\frac16+\frac14\right)=\frac{19}{144}.
\]
The formula recovers \(A_{21}=(19/144)/(19/36)=1/4\), and the covariance recursion recovers both entries of \(D=I_2\), so the recovered transfer is \(z/[4(1-z/3)]\).  The excluded condition is load-bearing: with
\[
 A(a)=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\a&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 D(a)=\operatorname{diag}(q_1,q_2-a^2q_1),
\]
where \(q_1,q_2>0\) and \(|a|<\sqrt{q_2/q_1}\), one has \(A(a)^3=0\) and
\[
 \sum_{r=0}^{2}A(a)^rD(a)(A(a)^r)^\top
 =\operatorname{diag}(q_1,q_2).
\]
Thus the same coarse law admits an open interval of transfers \(az\) when both endpoint persistences vanish.
